source: Minchat Shai on Gen 24:22 (the Masorah: 'לשתת — FOUR defective; their signs: until they finish drinking; they could not drink of the Nile; Marah; Rephidim'; the Ramah concurs)
claim_en: THE FOUR LEAN DRINKS: לשתת ('to drink,' defective) stands exactly FOUR times in the Torah, and they are precisely the Masorah's four — Rebecca's own offer ('until they have finished TO DRINK,' 24:19) and the three water-crises: the undrinkable Nile (Exod 7:24), Marah's bitterness (Exod 15:23), waterless Rephidim (Exod 17:1). The maiden's lean drink-word keeps company with the wilderness thirsts.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 24:22 ('when the camels had finished TO DRINK — plene vav in the precise books, the Hilleli, the old prints')
claim_en: ...and three verses later the narrator writes the same infinitive PLENE: כלו לשתות ('the camels had FINISHED drinking,' 24:22) — the offer lean, the fulfillment full, inside one scene, exactly as the precise books and the Hilleli rule against the printers.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 24:8 ('EVERY oath-noun in the Torah defective of vav — for every oath is from the word SEVEN'; Shaarei Orah, the second gate, cited: Abraham's seven ewes at Beer Sheva)
claim_en: THE OATH IS ALWAYS SEVEN: משבעתי ('you shall be clear of THIS MY OATH,' 24:8) — the oath-noun runs DEFECTIVE through the whole Torah (all ten tokens, builder-asserted lean), 'for every oath is from the word seven' (Shaarei Orah via Minchat Shai): the letters keep the oath indistinguishable from the seven — as at Beer Sheva, where the seven ewes sealed the swearing (21:28-31, the frozen well-oath unit).

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 24:14 ('הנערה is READ' — the qere note; the Zohar page named); the Masorah's Torah-wide maiden-rule
claim_en: THE MAIDEN WRITTEN AS THE LAD: הנער — at Rebecca's debut ('let THE MAIDEN to whom I say...,' 24:14) the consonants are the BOY-skeleton (no final heh) carrying GIRL-vowels: written one sex, read the other. SNAPSHOT instruments the whole rule: the vowel-only feminine skeleton stands at EIGHT Torah tokens (Rebecca's five in this chapter, Dinah's three in Gen 34, builder-asserted); the maiden-laws of Deut 22 pair an unpointed ktiv-token with its read-form; and in the WHOLE TORAH exactly ONE maiden is written out in full — Deut 22:19, where the slanderer must keep his bride ('she shall remain his wife'): the one place the letter writes her whole.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 24:16 (the qere note's second station)
claim_en: ...the second station verified: והנער ('and THE MAIDEN was very fair,' 24:16) — boy-skeleton, girl-vowels...

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 24:28 (the third station)
claim_en: ...the third: ותרץ הנער ('and THE MAIDEN ran to tell,' 24:28) — the same written lad, the same read maiden.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 24:33 ('written ויישם, read ויושם; the shuruk on the second yod — Masoret haMasoret: the qubutz-on-first reading is an outright error'; the Ramah concurs)
claim_en: THE SET-FOOD PAIR: ויישם ('and food WAS SET before him') — WRITTEN with two yods...

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 24:33 (the qere leg)
claim_en: ...and READ ויושם with the shuruk (the dotted vav) exactly where Masoret haMasoret demands it — SNAPSHOT carries both tokens, the written and the read, side by side.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 24:21 ('משתאה — the aleph with TZERE'; the Michlol page cited)
claim_en: משתאה ('the man GAZING at her, silent') — UNIQUE in the Torah, one token, and the aleph pointed tzere as the Michlol rules. The wonder-verb appears once in the letter, at the servant's watch.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 24:21 (the pointing leg)
claim_en: ...the tzere verified in the stream.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 24:2 ('המשל — the mem DAGESHED')
claim_en: המשל ('his servant... WHO RULED over all he had') — the mem carries dagesh (the doubling dot), as ruled: the ruling-word pressed on the trusted servant.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 24:5 ('הזאת — the zayin DAGESHED')
claim_en: הזאת ('to THIS land') — the zayin dageshed, as ruled.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 24:10 ('ויקם וילך — the revia on the yod of ויקם')
claim_en: ויקם ('and the servant AROSE and went') — the revia (the resting dot-accent) standing on the yod, as ruled.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 24:12 ('חסד — in the precise Sephardic books with ZAQEF GADOL')
claim_en: חסד ('show KINDNESS to my master Abraham' — the servant's prayer, the Torah's first prayer for a match) — under zaqef gadol (the great upright accent), exactly the precise-Sephardic reading. SNAPSHOT sides with the precise books.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 24:15 ('טרם — with ONE zarqa, on the mem alone')
claim_en: טרם ('BEFORE he had finished speaking — and behold, Rebecca') — one zarqa (the thrown-stone accent) on the mem alone, as ruled against the doubling editions: the before-word of the answered prayer carries a single ornament.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 24:15 ('ילדה — the Masorah troubled to mark it: UNIQUE, and defective'; the Ramah concurs; the dageshed lamed noted)
claim_en: ילדה ('Rebecca, who WAS BORN to Bethuel') — the passive born-form: dageshed lamed, no vav, and UNIQUE in the Torah (builder-asserted: one token of this pointing) — the Masorah marked it although the dagesh alone would forbid the vav, 'because it troubled to record: none like it.' The bride enters the letter through a one-of-a-kind birth-word.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 24:27 ('the FIRST אחי with tzere; the second — with chirik, at the retelling')
claim_en: בית אחי אדני ('the house of my master's BRETHREN' — the road-thanksgiving, 24:27) — אחי pointed TZERE: the plural construct, the whole kin-house; the Masorah's pair-note sends to the retelling (24:48, next unit's span) where the same consonants take CHIRIK — 'my master's BROTHER,' singular: one vowel widens or narrows the family.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 24:30 ('ואת הצמדים — for Ben Asher the vav carries the lengthener'; so in the precise Sephardic books)
claim_en: ואת ('and when he saw the nose-ring AND the bracelets') — the vav carrying the lengthener-stroke (meteg), the Ben Asher reading Minchat Shai matched in the Sephardic precise books. SNAPSHOT: the stroke stands.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 24:30 ('כה דבר — the dalet soft, the bet with SEGOL')
claim_en: כה דבר ('THUS SPOKE the man to me') — the dalet rafeh (soft, undotted) and the bet in segol, both as ruled: Laban's quotation-formula pointed exactly.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 24:4 ('one of FIVE verses that have no אם — and the erring insert it')
claim_en: THE MISSING BUT: כי אל־ארצי תלך ('BUT to my land you shall go,' 24:4) — one of the Masorah's FIVE verses where readers wrongly supply אם ('if/but') after כי: the verse has NO such token (builder-asserted verse scan) — the letter trusts כי alone to carry the turn.
